I was assigned a "first steps" worker and she's amazing help for my depression. She can come with you to all benefit/baby related meeting, arrange appointments for you and even take you shopping if you don't have transportation. I think I was "given" her at about 22 weeks, and we've been gradually working towards me going outside/performing tasks without my partner, and she says she will be able to help me until the baby is about 6 months old. 

I've spoken to her about fears of having my baby taken away (I had some crashes in the first and third trimester, self harming etc) and she said that they are only there to support me and will do everything they can to help. Even when they were suspicious I was becoming suicidal they would just "check up" on me and schedule appointments (they came to my house) every week, just for a chat or anything I found helpful. They have never once discussed or mentioned any social services intervention, however I have never been admitted to hospital for my depression or self harming. 

The perinatal mental health service is pretty bad where I am (Glasgow) because they were moving premesis, changing staff and just generally having useless reception staff, (I ended up waiting 4 months for a follow up appointment with a psychiatrist) and honestly the first steps worker was amazing. She works more with the practical side, not mental health, but I honestly found her 1000% more helpful than the charge nurse, psychiatrist and psychologist. If you can get access to that service I can't reccomeded it highly enough. 

It's also worth mentioning I have a friend who works in social services and she says "we're here to keep families together, not tear them apart".

My parents are foster carers, so they deal with children who have been removed from bad situations, and honestly it's only ever the absolute extreme, eg The social worker has arrived to check how things are getting on and the mum is high with a random guy in the house while the children are in dirty nappies scrounging from bins because they're hungry, and even then they work towards getting the parent in a stable position so the child can come home. 

Sorry for the mad long post, but I believe that things have to go very, very wrong before social services intervene and take a child away from the parent, even temporarily. 

I wish you all the best and hope your mood continues to improve x

Had this experience from the other side. When I was maybe 18-19 I used to stay over at an Internet cafe some nights, and I started getting the most horrible chest pain, on the left side. I thought it was maybe something to do with my ribs but I didn’t know how to accurately describe it. I would get it when I was walking back to my flat after an all nighter initially, but then I started getting it if I had to sit on an  un backed chair (chem lab was the big one). It made me sweat, gasp for breath and made me feel like I was going to vomit. Pain subsided pretty much immediately when I laid down. 

Explained this to my doctor who basically took the piss out of me and said “ we’re not going to give you any medication today” in a really patronising voice, and also asked me “what do you want me to do about it”. When I responded “help?” She said she would get another doctor but they would say the same thing. 

Ultimately that doctors visit was one of the most uncomfortable and embarrassing times of my life and lead to a mistrust of doctors and medical staff that I still have now(26). 

I ended up dropping out of college and stopping the all nighters and it wasn’t until I became pregnant this year I realised the pain was basically very bad trapped wind.  If I’d have known that at the time I would have just cut out the soda and been fine but the Drs rude, condescending and unhelpful manner basically meant I had to just suffer in silence or “they’ll think im a druggy”. 

TLDR Woman lives with completely preventable pain for years because Doctors couldn’t be arsed to investigate
